title: What If the Sun VANISHED Right Now? ☀️
description:
If the Sun vanished right now, you'd keep sunbathing for about eight minutes. Sunshine is light, and light takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to cross the 150 million kilometres from the Sun to you, so the sunshine already on its way would keep arriving. Changes in gravity travel at the speed of light too, so Earth would keep circling the empty spot for those same eight minutes. Then the sky would go dark, and Earth would fly off in a straight line at about 30 kilometres a second... and you wouldn't feel a thing, because you and Earth are falling together. (Relax: the Sun can't actually vanish.) Panic or keep sunbathing?

How do we know gravity is that fast? In 2017 two neutron stars collided 130 million light-years away, and their gravitational waves and their light arrived 1.7 seconds apart.
